source.title: DiCoDe: Diffusion-Compressed Deep Tokens for Autoregressive Video Generation with Language Models
source.authors: Yi-Zhuo Li; Yu-Ying Ge; Yixiao Ge; Ping Luo; Shan Ying

record.file_problem: Whole paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent cut-off.
record.tranche_reason: Tests model-size trends in an autoregressive video-generation setting, a modality and training regime beyond text pretraining. It does not reproduce the original held-out cross-entropy scaling measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a model-size sweep and states that larger models have lower pre-training loss and lower FVD. It does not fit or report power-law exponents, and the plotted values are not stated numerically. The single-model MSR-VTT comparison in Table 2 does not test a scale trend; comparisons to other methods there are not scale-sweep results.
record.test_reason: The study reports a five-point model-size sweep (117M to 3.21B) of text-pretrained GPT2 and Llama3.2 models trained on continuous video tokens under one fixed setting. It reports final GMM training loss and MSR-VTT FVD. This is a new-modality result on whether loss and downstream quality improve with size. It is weak evidence: there is no power-law fit, values are figure-only, the loss is training loss, size is confounded with model family and text pretraining, and the Llama models are unconverged.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors claim clear scalability from 100M to 3B (lower loss and FVD with size at the same budget). They also say the GPT2–Llama3.2 gap shows text knowledge transfers to video, and that Llama3.2 models are unconverged and could improve with more training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GMM loss for continuous video tokens and evaluates video-generation FVD, rather than fitting held-out text cross-entropy scaling laws or optimizing a fixed-compute parameter/token split.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family affects results: the paper attributes a gap between GPT2 and Llama3.2 to better Llama3.2 pre-training. The loss curves also show that Llama3.2 models are far from convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched training budget, Llama3.2 models show a clear loss and FVD gap over GPT2 models, attributed to better text pretraining transferring to video.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Text-pretraining quality of the initialisation shifts video-generation loss beyond parameter count.

record.problems: No power-law fitting or exponents; no held-out cross-entropy results; plotted scale-sweep values are not numerically stated; the authors report that the Llama3.2 models are far from convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's single DiCoDe-Llama3.2-1B MSR-VTT result (CLIPSIM 0.2950, FVD 367) is not a scale comparison and does not establish predictability. The other methods in that table are comparison results, not this study's scale-sweep outcomes.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents and range over several orders of magnitude in video. Held-out loss. Data or compute scaling. Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning regimes as such.
Quantitative predictability of FVD from scale or loss. Downstream tasks other than MSR-VTT FVD.
Not tested: no text held-out loss.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small runs.
Not tested: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Not tested: no fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The figure labels GPT2-Large as 774M while the text says 762M, and Llama3.2-3B as 3.21B while the text says 3.3B. Tables 3 and 4 are tokenizer and loss-type ablations at fixed 1B size, not scale results. Excluding Table 2 is correct. The record's original labels cited untested parts (no power-law fit) as limits_scope; the labels are revised to rest on the family confound and non-convergence instead.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out cross-entropy power laws for language-model pretraining in parameters, tokens, or compute; the reported objective is GMM loss on continuous video tokens, with no held-out cross-entropy or power-law fit.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run losses.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The video setting is tested only for a qualitative loss trend across model sizes; no power-law form, fit, or exponent is tested. Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer are not tested.
Reports a qualitative FVD trend with model size, but no quantitative prediction from scale or pretraining loss and no other downstream tasks.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or curve bending.

conditions.value: 117M to 3.21B, across GPT2 and Llama3.2 families

rows.value: figure only; text states that larger models achieve lower pre-training loss
rows.note: The plotted loss values are not numerically stated. The paper reports a decreasing trend, but does not establish a power law; it also says Llama3.2 models are far from convergence.
rows.check: Loss falls with size, but no power-law form or exponent is tested and values are figure-only. The measure is final training (pre-training) GMM loss, not held-out loss. Size is confounded with family (GPT2 vs Llama3.2, which the authors say differ in pretraining quality). Llama models are 'far from convergence', so training budget is a bottleneck. The range spans only about 1.4 orders of magnitude.

relationships.condition: DiCoDe video-token AR models initialised from text LMs (GPT2 117M–774M, Llama3.2 1.23B–3.21B), same training budget
relationships.reason: R1: loss falls with size, but the authors attribute a clear GPT2/Llama3.2 gap to text pretraining quality, so loss depends on initialisation, not size alone. Llama runs are unconverged.
relationships.display_finding: Loss fell with size, but the authors attributed the GPT2–Llama3.2 gap to pretraining quality, and Llama runs had not converged.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot MSR-VTT FVD for the same size sweep
relationships.reason: R2: FVD improves monotonically with size, but the improvement is entangled with the model-family change and unconverged training. No predictive fit is reported.
relationships.display_finding: FVD improved monotonically, although model-family changes and unconverged training confounded the size comparison, and no predictive relationship was fitted.
